extracted text: The aluminum alloys used in this study were rolled Al 7075-T6 and Al 2024-T3 sheets 2 mm in thickness (termed 'D' and 'L', respectively), and Al 1050-H24 sheets (termed 'H') 0.5 mm in thickness. According to Table II notes, T6 = solution treating followed by quenching and finally peak age hardening; T3 = solution treating followed by quenching, cold working, and finally natural aging; and H24 = work hardening followed by partial annealing (240 °C). The composition is given in atomic percent in Table I. For the 1050 alloy, some values are reported as less than a certain value (<0.005 or <0.010).
property mapping:
AA: Aluminum Association designation (7075, 2024, 1050)
temper: Heat treatment designation (T6, T3, H24)
YS [MPa]: Yield Strength in megapascals (YS column in Table II)
UTS [MPa]: Ultimate Tensile Strength in megapascals (UTS column in Table II)
elong [%]: Elongation percentage (Elongation column in Table II)
Hardness: Vickers hardness (HV column in Table II)
Hardness UNIT: HV (Vickers hardness)
Has composition: True (composition is specified in Table I)
abbreviations:
D: Designation for Al 7075-T6 sheets
L: Designation for Al 2024-T3 sheets
H: Designation for Al 1050-H24 sheets
T6: Solution treating followed by quenching and peak age hardening
T3: Solution treating followed by quenching, cold working, and natural aging
H24: Work hardening followed by partial annealing at 240°C
UTS: Ultimate tensile strength
YS: Yield stress
HV: Vickers hardness
Pct: Percent
